whatItIs.text: The knobbly rhizome of a tropical plant, related to turmeric and cardamom; used fresh, dried, and ground as both spice and folk remedy.

historyNote.text: Ginger originated in Maritime Southeast Asia and is a true cultigen with no wild form; Austronesian voyagers carried it across the Pacific from around 5,000 years ago, making it one of the first spices exported from Asia.

howToChoose.text: Choose rhizomes that feel firm and heavy with smooth, taut skin; wrinkled or shrivelled pieces are dried out and fibrous.

storage.text: Keep unwrapped in the crisper, or freeze whole and grate from frozen.

useItUp.text: Cut ginger freezes well and grates beautifully from frozen; simmer bruised slices into tea, or candy the peel-off cuts.

substitutions.note: warmer and drier; best in bakes, not stir-fries
